verdicts.evidence: The problem is equivalent to finding $p \in \mathbb{Q}^+$ such that there exist $d_n \in \{0, \pm 1, \pm 2\}$, not all zero, such that $\sum_{n=1}^N d_n p^n = 0$. If $p=a/b$ in simplest form, this implies $a$ must divide $d_k$ (the first non-zero coefficient) and $b$ must divide $d_N$ (the last non-zero coefficient). Thus $a, b \in \{1, 2\}$, which means $p \in \{1/2, 1, 2\}$. All these values were verified to work.
